findings.text: Remote coverage collection is offered through operations named kcov_remote_start and kcov_remote_stop together with a query named kcov_common_handle yielding a common handle identifier. Start validates handle and context before attaching a buffer, stop detaches and merges, and the query reports zero outside task context.

Coverage control is exposed as a file interface collected in table kcov_fops whose operations connect open handling named kcov_open and ioctl handling named kcov_ioctl and address mapping named kcov_mmap and release named kcov_close. Initialization creates a privileged debug entry for that interface and prepopulates a pool of interrupt safe areas sized by configuration, optionally running a power on self check.

Image lifecycle is managed through operations named sanity_check_segment_list and do_kimage_alloc_init and kimage_terminate and kimage_free and kimage_load_segment together with file mode cleanup named kimage_file_post_load_cleanup. Validation checks descriptors, allocation builds a control object, termination marks the entry chain, release frees the object, and loading handles one segment by index.

A mode counts as enabled whenever its value ignoring a context switch flag differs from the disabled value. Predicates named kcov_mode_enabled and constants named KCOV_IN_CTXSW and KCOV_MODE_DISABLED express this test, which gates preservation of task state and rejection of nested start in task context and early exit from stop.

Remote start proceeds only in task context or genuine soft interrupt context, rejects nested use in tasks with active tracing and repeated entry while already marked in soft interrupt service, and ends silently when handle lookup misses. Misuse cases produce warnings rather than corrupting state.

For task context the session uses a remote configured size with a shareable pooled buffer, while soft interrupt context uses a fixed configuration size with an interrupt safe pooled buffer. The chosen area count is cleared before collection begins, and sizing constants include CONFIG_KCOV_IRQ_AREA_SIZE and a per owner remote size.

Entering a soft interrupt session preserves interrupted task tracing mode and size and area pointer and sequence and owner, then halts current collection and marks soft interrupt ownership. Leaving clears the mark and reattaches the preserved session, then clears all preserved fields. Fields involved include kcov_mode and kcov_size and kcov_area and kcov_sequence and kcov and kcov_softirq plus saved counterparts.

Merging copies entries from a source area into free space of a destination area without overflow, supporting program counter and comparison record shapes with different header widths and entry codings. The logic bounds destination length, computes occupied and free bytes with shifts rather than division, copies only what fits, issues an ordering barrier, then publishes the increased count. Modes involved are KCOV_MODE_TRACE_PC and KCOV_MODE_TRACE_CMP with grouping KCOV_WORDS_PER_CMP.

Stop snapshots owner and area and size and sequence, halts collection, restores any soft interrupt predecessor, then merges into the owner buffer only when the snapshot sequence still matches the owner sequence and the owner remains in remote mode. The temporary area is always returned to the pool and a reference acquired at start is released.
The common handle query reports zero when the caller is not in task context and otherwise reports the handle stored in the current task structure under field kcov_handle.

Ordinary control commands execute with the instance spin lock held with interrupt state saved, acquired around the locked ioctl helper and released before freeing a temporary argument and yielding the result.

Remote start and stop serialize per processor state with a local lock that also saves interrupt state, and protect the remote table with a separate spin lock. Owner fields are sampled while holding the table lock because the instance lock cannot be taken there without risking deadlock due to opposite acquisition order elsewhere.

Merging into the owner buffer happens under the owner instance lock, while pooled area retrieval and return happen under the remote table lock. Startup seeding of the pool uses the interrupt saving form of the table lock.

A remote session moves from idle through validation and table lookup with reference acquisition and buffer provision and soft interrupt preservation when relevant and attachment, then at stop through detachment and predecessor restoration and conditional merge and pool return and reference release. Missing handles or disabled modes or unmatched soft interrupt marks abort without state change.

When no pooled buffer is available and the caller may sleep, the start path drops the per processor lock, allocates a fresh buffer dynamically, and reacquires the lock, while interrupt context never sleeps for this. Allocation failure releases the previously acquired owner reference and leaves no session attached.

Task tracing state comprises fields named kcov_mode and kcov_size and kcov_area and kcov_sequence and kcov and kcov_softirq and kcov_handle, plus preserved copies named kcov_saved_mode and kcov_saved_size and kcov_saved_area and kcov_saved_sequence and kcov_saved_kcov used across nested soft interrupt sessions.

Segment validation requires page aligned start and end with no wraparound and below a destination limit, pairwise non overlap, buffered size not exceeding memory size, and total plus per segment page counts within half of system memory computed with upward rounding. Crash images additionally require containment within a reserved crash region, and every destination range is accepted before swapping.

Allocation checks that a panic entry lies inside the crash reservation, allocates a zeroed control object, records entry and segment descriptors, marks panic images with a crash type and a reserved control page, validates the list, reserves a control code page sized by a control constant, and for non panic images also reserves a single swap page, unwinding on any failure.

Loading serializes with a try lock, selects crash or normal destination, treats a zero segment count as uninstall, clears any prior crash image when loading a new panic image, then allocates and applies preservation and hotplug options and prepares machine state and copies crash metadata and loads each segment and terminates the chain and runs post load machine handling and installs the new image by exchange and restores crash protection and frees the displaced image.

A fresh control object links entry cursors named entry and last_entry to head, uses an all ones sentinel for control_page meaning no control page, selects default type, initializes collections named control_pages and dest_pages and unusable_pages as empty, and when hotplug is configured selects none action with an invalid header index and a cleared updated flag in fields named hp_action and elfcorehdr_index and elfcorehdr_updated.

Termination advances past a nonzero current slot and then stores a completion marker. Iteration walks from the head following indirection entries through address translation and stopping at either a zero slot or the completion marker. Markers involved are named IND_DONE and IND_INDIRECTION and IND_SOURCE.

Release treats absent objects as no ops, unmaps and clears any copied crash metadata, frees destination and unusable collections, walks the entry chain freeing a prior indirection page when a new indirection is met and freeing source pages directly, frees the final indirection, runs machine cleanup, frees control pages and contiguous allocations, and when in file mode releases temporary load buffers.

File mode cleanup releases kernel image and initial filesystem and command line and purgatory image and section header buffers plus measurement state when present, delegates architecture specific and loader owned data release, nulls each pointer after release, and clears a debug printing flag. A header provides an empty inline variant of the same operation for configurations without file loading.

Segment loading dispatches on image type to a normal path helper by default and to a crash path helper for crash images when crash support is configured, yielding an allocation failure code when no path applies.

Coverage parameters include disabled value named KCOV_MODE_DISABLED and flag named KCOV_IN_CTXSW and tracing modes named KCOV_MODE_TRACE_PC and KCOV_MODE_TRACE_CMP and grouping named KCOV_WORDS_PER_CMP and interrupt area sizing named CONFIG_KCOV_IRQ_AREA_SIZE and a self test duration of a few hundred milliseconds.

Loading parameters include flags named KEXEC_ON_CRASH and KEXEC_PRESERVE_CONTEXT and types named KEXEC_TYPE_DEFAULT and KEXEC_TYPE_CRASH and control sizing named KEXEC_CONTROL_PAGE_SIZE and destination limit named KEXEC_DESTINATION_MEMORY_LIMIT and page constants named PAGE_MASK and PAGE_SHIFT and PAGE_SIZE and hotplug none action named KEXEC_CRASH_HP_NONE and entry markers named IND_DONE and IND_INDIRECTION and IND_SOURCE.

Concurrent loads are rejected as busy when the global lock is already held. Uninstall exchanges the destination pointer with null and frees the old image. Crash protection is removed before replacing a crash image and restored afterward when a crash image remains.

Startup seeds one pooled interrupt area per possible processor, with extra slots under a real time configuration, and fails initialization when any allocation fails. The optional self check enables tracing without a buffer while spinning on a timer so that any stray interrupt tracing would fault, then disables tracing.
